metadata.title: Tobacco Industry System Components
metadata.description: Network diagram showing interconnections in the tobacco industry

nodes.label:
Tobacco
Companies
nodes.description: Major tobacco corporations (Philip Morris, BAT, etc.) that manufacture and distribute tobacco products globally.
nodes.title: Tobacco Companies

nodes.label:
Advertising
Agencies
nodes.description: Marketing firms that create campaigns to promote tobacco products and shape public perception.
nodes.title: Advertising Agencies

nodes.label:
Retail
Outlets
nodes.description: Stores, gas stations, and vendors that sell tobacco products directly to consumers.
nodes.title: Retail Outlets

nodes.label:
Tobacco
Farmers
nodes.description: Agricultural workers who grow tobacco, often economically dependent on the industry.
nodes.title: Tobacco Farmers

nodes.label:
Regulatory
Agencies
nodes.description: FDA, FTC, and other agencies responsible for tobacco regulation and enforcement.
nodes.title: Regulatory Agencies (FDA, etc.)

nodes.label:
Tax
Authorities
nodes.description: Government bodies that collect tobacco taxes—a significant revenue source.
nodes.title: Tax Authorities

nodes.label:
Public Health
Departments
nodes.description: Government agencies focused on population health and anti-smoking campaigns.
nodes.title: Public Health Departments

nodes.label: Legislators
nodes.description: Elected officials who create tobacco-related laws and receive industry lobbying.
nodes.title: Legislators

nodes.label:
Healthcare
Systems
nodes.description: Hospitals, clinics, and providers treating smoking-related diseases.
nodes.title: Healthcare Systems

nodes.label:
Insurance
Companies
nodes.description: Health insurers who bear costs of tobacco-related illnesses.
nodes.title: Insurance Companies

nodes.label:
Medical
Researchers
nodes.description: Scientists studying tobacco health effects—sometimes industry-funded.
nodes.title: Medical Researchers

nodes.label:
Treatment
Providers
nodes.description: Smoking cessation programs and addiction treatment specialists.
nodes.title: Treatment Providers

nodes.label:
Consumers
(Smokers)
nodes.description: Adult tobacco users who purchase and consume products.
nodes.title: Consumers/Smokers

nodes.label: Youth
nodes.description: Potential new users—primary target for industry growth strategies.
nodes.title: Youth (Potential New Users)

nodes.label:
Advocacy
Groups
nodes.description: Anti-smoking organizations and public health advocates.
nodes.title: Advocacy Groups

nodes.label: Media
nodes.description: News outlets and entertainment that shape public perception of smoking.
nodes.title: Media

nodes.label:
Cigarettes
Vapes
nodes.description: Tobacco products including traditional cigarettes, e-cigarettes, and vaping devices.
nodes.title: Cigarettes and Vapes

edges.label: Purchases
edges.description: Consumer purchases of tobacco and vaping products

edges.label: Produces
edges.description: Companies manufacture cigarettes and vaping products

edges.label: Taxes
edges.description: Tobacco and vape product taxes collected at point of sale

regulatory_capture.title: Regulatory Capture
regulatory_capture.text: Industry lobbying can lead to regulators serving industry interests rather than public health.

information_asymmetry.title: Information Asymmetry
information_asymmetry.text: Industry has more information about product harms than consumers, creating an unfair advantage.

externalized_costs.title: Externalized Costs
externalized_costs.text: Healthcare costs of smoking are borne by consumers and society, not the industry.
